title: Development and pilot testing of a strategy for identifying expressions of wishes to hasten death die in routine clinical documentation (EPSIT): A retrospective chart review
summary:
This project investigates the feasibility of systematically identifying and differentiating expressions of a wish to hasten death (WTHD) in routine clinical documentation, using patient records from the palliative care and psychiatric departments at the University Hospital of Cologne. Its primary aim is to develop and pilot a reproducible search and coding strategy for identifying and classifying different forms of wishes to hasten death in unstructured clinical documentation.
In addition, the project will explore the feasibility of identifying such expressions in routine clinical data and examine current documentation practices. This analysis will focus on the linguistic manifestations of wishes to hasten death, the professional groups documenting them, and the clinical contexts in which they occur, particularly in relation to requests for assisted suicide. Clinical responses to documented wishes to hasten death, including specialist consultations and therapeutic interventions, will also be described.
In the longer term, the project aims to establish a methodological foundation for future multicenter studies investigating the care of patients expressing a wish to hasten death.
conditions: Documentation of wishes to hasten death

interventions.name: This is a single-center, exploratory, retrospective medical record review examining expressions of the wish to hasten death in routine clinical documentation. The study is based on patient records from the Center for Palliative Medicine and the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy at Universit

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Only completed treatment cases (discharge or death) are included in order to analyze complete documentation histories.
-    Treatment in one of the participating units (palliative care or psychiatry) during the defined study period
-    Availability of routine documentation
To increase the likelihood of identifying patients with complex care needs (TW), n = 20 cases (n = 10 each from palliative care and psychiatry) are specifically selected that exhibit at least one of the following characteristics:
-    Documented high symptom burden (IPOS, HOPE; at least 2 of the domains “physical,” “psychological,” “social,” or “spiritual” are affected)
-    Complex clinical courses involving a multidisciplinary team, particularly with psychiatric or palliative care consultation
-    Involvement of psychosocial (social services, pastoral care, psychologists) or psycho-oncological services
Exclusion criteria:
There are no exclusion criteria
